answer: A mechanism that actually bites: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because onyx only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, terrace is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any horizon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
